name: Do I need a glass door on a walk-in shower, or can I leave it open?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a glass door on a walk-in shower, or can I leave it open?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Shower doors are optional; a fixed glass panel, curtain, or open entry may work depending on splash direction, room size, ventilation, and the user’s ability to operate a door. Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate glass and enclosure decisions with the shower layout rather than treating them as a late add-on.

An open entry may feel spacious but can send water onto the bathroom floor if the spray and slope are not carefully planned.

Key factors:
- Showerhead direction and entry location
- Available splash zone
- Cleaning preferences
- Door clearance and accessibility

Ask for a plan showing the spray, glass, and entry path. Confirm whether glass measurement occurs after finished surfaces are installed.

The best enclosure balances water control with ease of use.
acceptedAnswer.description: You do not always need a door. A fixed panel, curtain, or open entry can work when the shower size, spray direction, slope, and ventilation control splash. Review the glass and entry layout together before choosing an enclosure.
